notes: All latency budgets must also hold under a 4x CPU-throttled profile (CDP throttling).
Per execution-plan E5, the CI gate is relative-first (extension on vs off in the same job); absolute values are secondary tripwires.
Budgets are enforced from M3; at M0 this file is plumbing — scripts/perf-harness.mjs only reads and reports it.

RATIFIED 2026-10-11 (user decision, M3 gate): the former memory-growth-5000-cycles entry (budget 0, comparison '~', unit 'slope' — 'no positive leak slope') is replaced by two explicit bounds: total growth over 5,000 cycles < 2 MB, and leak slope <= 0.03 KB/cycle. Calibration: observed slope was 0.010–0.011 KB/cycle in CI and ~0.015 KB/cycle (15 B/cycle) locally — the slope bound is 2x the worst observed value; observed total growth was ~60 KB in CI and +93 KB locally, ~20x inside the 2 MB bound (which the harness already evaluated implicitly and is now an explicit budget entry). The literal-zero slope could never pass; the ratified pair still catches a real leak immediately.

RATIFIED 2026-10-11 (user decision, M3 gate): latency gating methodology. Shared-CI-runner noise swung the single-shot throttled p95 from +97.5/+92.3 ms (fail) to -43 ms (pass) on equivalent code, and the warm median flickered to 10.351 ms against its <10 ms budget. The latency budget NUMBERS are unchanged (<10 ms median, <25 ms p95); the harness now runs 5 rounds of extension-on vs extension-off per profile (warm and 4x-throttled; cold stays informational and single-shot) and gates on the median across rounds. All rounds run and are reported — the median decides; there are no retries-until-pass.

FOLLOW-UP 2026-10-11 (user decision, M3 gate): the ratification run (PR #2, run 38152995111) failed on exactly one row — throttled added-latency p95 under median-of-rounds, 101.07 ms vs the unchanged <25 ms budget. Per-round p95 deltas were -116.21, +203.64, +107.91, +5.11, +101.07 ms: differencing two tail percentiles over ~39 samples per round under 4x throttling is noise-dominated, and with three of five rounds > +100 ms the median inherited the noise (the throttled median gated at -5.54 ms and the warm rows passed comfortably). The throttled p95 gate statistic is now a POOLED percentile: all rounds' raw samples are pooled per condition (extension-on together, extension-off together, ~195 samples per pool at 5 rounds), one p95 is computed per pool, and the gate is pooled-p95(on) minus pooled-p95(off) against the same <25 ms budget. Warm median/p95 and the throttled median keep median-of-rounds; the superseded throttled median-of-rounds p95 and the per-round p95 deltas are still reported informationally. No budget number changed.

DESIGN CHANGE 2026-10-11 (user decision, M3 gate): latency measurement design. PR #3's run (38158520765) passed the pooled throttled p95 (-37.7 ms) but the throttled added-latency MEDIAN failed at 21.61 ms vs the <10 ms budget — a row that read -5.54 ms in PR #2's run on unchanged extension code. Sequential per-round blocks (a full baseline browser run, then a full extension browser run, minutes apart) let shared-runner drift sign the delta, and the block design's run-to-run swing (~±30 ms) exceeds the budget it enforces. The latency scenario now measures with two live browsers per profile in interleaved ABBA blocks (~5 tab-opens per block, alternating extension-off / on / on / off): within each ABBA quartet the two conditions' time centroids coincide, so linear drift cancels in the paired difference. The added-latency MEDIAN (warm and throttled) gates on the median of the paired block differences (per-quartet paired deltas pooled across rounds); warm p95 keeps the ratified median-of-rounds; the throttled p95 keeps the pooled-percentile statistic over the interleaved samples. The superseded median-of-rounds statistics remain reported informationally. Warm-up: one unmeasured warm-up block per browser per round replaces the per-batch first-tab discard for the interleaved profiles (cold keeps the first-tab discard). The latency batches are now UNIQUE-ONLY: duplicate opens (previously 25% of each batch) resolve by detach in the extension condition but by full load in the baseline, contaminating the added-latency estimand; the duplicate path keeps its own duplicate-focus-swap budget and scenario. NO BUDGET NUMBER CHANGED — the <10 ms median and <25 ms p95 budgets stand exactly as ratified.
